mustPassLedger.pattern: 'Mark a line across the pitch | a target zone | Set out gates of two cones — beyond the first defenders | behind the pressing players'

selfCheck:
INPUT NOTE: the brief names three proposals, but only two were supplied, NOISE-FIRST (3 procedures) and REPRESENTATION-FIRST (2 procedures). The defect-first set was not in the input, so this reconciliation covers two.

STRUCTURE DECISION: 2 procedures, split by which sentence class is at fault, not by failure mode. Representation-first split by determinacy vs capacity, which leaves a seam readers could fall into: '10 players in a 6v6 format' can be read as a conflict (GA-1) or a total (GA-2). Noise-first's separate SPACE and ROSTER procedures share one root fact (declarations do not resolve to one configuration inside the envelope), so they are merged into GA-LAYOUT. GA-LAYOUT reads only declaration templates and roster tokens. GA-PLAY reads only X1 (c)-(f). No sentence pattern is read by both, and X9 suppression stops GA-PLAY re-reporting a referent into a failed layout or roster.

DEFECT LEDGER WALK (39 rows, 31 activities rejected, 29 pass):
- D01-D03: GA-LAYOUT steps 4-5, lengthwise group (54 > 30; 36 + central > 30; 36 > 30). GA-PLAY sees 'middle'/'wide' in the same activities as suppressed names; 'deep' is not a band of the failed group, so it is reported separately (D09, D16, D21). Different facts, one owner each.
- D04: step 1, no template. GA-PLAY D30 in the same activity reads the roster, not that declaration, so it is not suppressed. Independent.
- D05-D08: step 7, one L-ROSTER each. D07's and D08's 'extra numbers' are suppressed in GA-PLAY under X9(b). em-foundation-neutral s3's 'extra numbers' is suppressed too. D20's 'deep' is a place referent, so the roster failure does not suppress it.
- D09-D27: GA-PLAY step 5, the 'deep' name, one per activity. Verified 19 of 60 by script; emphasis-applying s1 is the only slot 1 without the sentence.
- D28-D32: step 5, X8 step 4, one group finding each. D31 depends on the 6v6 default (X2). D32 merges three sites.
- D33-D35: step 3 P-EFFECT, so processing stops and 'opposite' is not reported again as P-REFERENT.
- D36-D37: step 6, TURNOVER, RELOCATE vs CONTINUE. The other statements in those activities resolve, so the comparison is not blocked.
- D38-D39: step 3, two distinct statements.
No row is caught by two procedures, and no row is caught twice inside GA-PLAY.

MUST-PASS WALK: every item was traced against X1-X8. No GA-LAYOUT template misfires on the 26 layout instances. ps-wide s1's second sentence joins the corridor group, giving 5 + 20 + 5. Every boilerplate intersection holds, including the sideline, the circle and the middle crosswise band. em-shaping-wide-zone s2 'restarts with a quick transition after a turnover' leaves the mode unstated, so there is no conflict. The rpc s1 and ls-first-time s1 'Use the goalkeeper to reset play' lines are tactical under the X1 verb rule. gf-positional s2 passes (START from the boilerplate; AFTER-SCORE default). emphasis-applying s1-s2 pass (goal kick). scoring-swapped s3 passes GA-LAYOUT and fails only D31.

WHERE THIS SET OVERRULES A PROPOSAL, AND WHY:
(1) gf-positional s2: representation-first failed it on unresolved ends. Its own S9 derives ends from any 'own half' statement, and the boilerplate is one, so the failure was internally inconsistent. It passes here.
(2) emphasis-applying s3 30-second window: representation-first admitted a default reading (S19). This set requires a stated start trigger and expiry effect for novel mechanics, because no coaching convention fixes them (turnover vs score-void). The first-pass finding was upheld by its challenger. Kept as D38.
(3) ls-reinforcing s3: noise-first said 'two tables, not admitted'; this set uses representation-first's deterministic additive reading (13). Same verdict, but a fixed arithmetic reason.
(4) 'gets the opposite channel': noise-first typed it as an untyped effect, representation-first as an unresolved referent. Effect-first ordering was chosen, so it is one finding either way.
(5) Noise-first said 20 slot-3 activities carry 'extra numbers'; the script shows 19 (not emphasis-applying s3).
(6) Noise-first's FAIL-OBJECTIVE step and representation-first's separate conflict and capacity steps are folded into step 5 or step 6.

HAND-VERIFIED ITEMS: all 3 geometry and all 3 roster items are in the ledger. 'deep' 19 of 19. 'extraNumbersInEvenGame' 3 is extended to 5 by the default and the alias merge (scoring-swapped s3, ps-none s3). 'goalKickWithoutGoals' 3 and 'noStartOrRestartStated' 2 are counts, not rulings: the first is admitted (MP-RESTART-WORDS), and both activities in the second state a start in Rules.

THINGS THAT DO NOT FULLY WORK:
(a) The X3 and X1 lexicons are closed. A correct but new phrasing in a future activity will fail until it is added. That is deliberate, and it reports as a finding rather than a silent pass.
(b) The boilerplate scope choice (START + AFTER-SCORE + AFTER-OUT vs START + AFTER-SCORE) changes no verdict on these 60, so the corpus cannot test it.
(c) info-variable-target s3 'Create a central overload by having one team.' is a truncated sentence that passes only because it is tactical by verb. A garbled declaration that starts with 'Create a <region>' would fail, but this one does not.
(d) Unexercised steps (GA-LAYOUT step 3 negation contradiction; GA-PLAY placement count against the roster) are stated but not validated by any instance.
openRisks: X1 trigger-sentence classification is still where careful readers are most likely to split. 'Use the goalkeeper to reset play when possession is lost' (rpc s1) could be read as a stoppage RELOCATE, which would add a TURNOVER conflict with 'No reset, no stoppage'. The rule (imperative behaviour verb, no 'from <place>' → tactical) decides it, but a reader who weighs 'reset' as a restart word would disagree.

D38 (30-second window) against an admitted value-gate reading: a reader who accepts 'a score counts only within 30 s of gaining possession' as ordinary coach shorthand would pass it. The deciding line in this set is that novel mechanics get no default effect.
D28-D31 ('extra numbers' in 6v6) depend on refusing the local-overload reading. A coach might run a local-superiority bonus by eye, so some readers will call this subjective rather than structural.
D31 (scoring-swapped s3) depends on the 6v6 roster default. A reader tempted to split 12 as 7v5 because the title says 'Overload' would pass it, but that reads the title, which X0 excludes.
D08 (ls-reinforcing s3) is not among the hand-verified rosters. A reader who takes 'with an extra attacker for the team in possession' as describing the 7th of a fixed 7v5 gets a legal table of 12.

gf-positional s3 'Play 7v5 for the attacking team' passes as fixed 7v5. It could also mean 5v5 plus 2 floaters for whoever attacks: also 12, but a different table. X2 decides it, but the text genuinely supports both.

D33-D35: a reader who types 'the other team gets the opposite channel' as ACCESS would report the defect as an unresolved 'opposite' instead of an untyped effect. The count stays the same, but the label differs.

Admitted table policies that change hand counts and need owner sign-off: 'goal kick' with no goals (emphasis-applying s1-s3); the negation scope in baseline s2 and em-consequence-progression s2 (a first-pass finding on baseline s2 was upheld); the kick-off convention (ps-goal-kicks s2); the boilerplate's scope.

X3 'zones' with no list and no axis word fails to parse. No activity exercises it, but the rule is strict, and a future 'Divide the field into three zones.' would fail although many coaches would read thirds.
'Play begins with a pass from the defending team' (baseline s2) is resolved as a coin-toss role. A reader could call a start by the 'defending' team incoherent.
